_about: Hand-written field-mark cards, the input scripts/build.py turns into prompts. DRAFT: written from general field-guide knowledge, not yet checked against references or by mammalogists. Keyed by iNaturalist scientific name. pose: one of the keys in POSES in scripts/build.py. similar: the look-alike the model is most likely to draw instead.

Odocoileus virginianus.draw: adult male (buck) in reddish-brown summer coat, with full hard antlers
Odocoileus virginianus.marks: antlers: one main beam on each side that sweeps forward, with unbranched tines rising straight up from it; white ring around the eye and nose band, white throat patch; broad tail about the length of the head, brown above with a white fringe and pure white below, held down; white belly and inner legs; large ears about half the head length
Odocoileus virginianus.difference: antler tines rise from one forward-curving beam (mule deer antlers fork into two, then fork again); tail long and brown above with white edges (mule deer: short, white with a black tip); ears smaller than a mule deer's

Sciurus carolinensis.marks: back and sides silver-grey with a brownish wash along the spine and on the feet; belly white to pale grey, sharply divided from the grey sides; very bushy tail as long as the body, grey with a white frosted fringe, raised in an S-curve over the back; pale eye-ring; small rounded ears without tufts
Sciurus carolinensis.difference: grey, not red; ears rounded with no tufts; tail edged with white frosting; larger and heavier than the Eurasian Red Squirrel

Odocoileus hemionus.draw: adult male (buck) in grey-brown coat, with full hard antlers
Odocoileus hemionus.marks: very large mule-like ears, about two thirds the head length; antlers fork into two equal branches, each of which forks again; white rump patch; short thin white tail with a black tip; dark V or patch on the forehead; white throat patch; stocky body
Odocoileus hemionus.difference: antlers branch by forking (not tines on one beam); huge ears; short white tail with a black tip (white-tailed deer: long brown tail with a white fringe)

Sylvilagus floridanus.draw: adult, crouched on all four feet in the typical resting posture
Sylvilagus floridanus.marks: grey-brown agouti fur; rust-brown nape patch behind the ears; ears about the head length, held up, with no black tips; tail a white cotton ball on the underside, brown above; large dark eye with a pale ring; long hind feet
Sylvilagus floridanus.difference: rusty nape patch; slimmer and smaller than the European Rabbit; ears without black tips

Procyon lotor.marks: black mask across the eyes edged with white above and below; bushy tail about half the body length with five to seven black rings on grey-buff; grizzled grey coat; pointed muzzle with a dark band down the nose; rounded ears edged white; hind legs longer than front legs so the rump is higher than the shoulders; dark, hand-like front paws with long fingers
Procyon lotor.difference: black eye mask; tail shorter and bushier than a coati's, held low, not upright; muzzle short, not long and flexible

Sciurus niger.draw: adult of the common orange-bellied eastern form
Sciurus niger.marks: back grizzled grey-brown; belly, cheeks and feet rusty orange; very bushy tail as long as the body, orange-brown with a tawny fringe, raised in a curve over the back; no white eye-ring; largest tree squirrel in its range
Sciurus niger.difference: orange belly and orange tail fringe; the Eastern Gray Squirrel has a white belly and a white-frosted tail

Vulpes vulpes.draw: adult of the common red form
Vulpes vulpes.marks: orange-red coat; white chin, throat and chest; legs and the backs of the ears black, like black stockings; very bushy tail about two thirds of the body length, held straight out, ending in a white tip; narrow pointed muzzle; large pointed ears; amber eyes with vertical slit pupils
Vulpes vulpes.difference: orange-red, black lower legs, white tail tip (gray fox: grizzled grey back, black-tipped tail with a black stripe along the top)

Canis latrans.marks: grizzled grey-buff coat with a darker saddle; tawny legs, muzzle and ears; whitish throat and belly; narrow, pointed muzzle; large pointed ears; bushy tail about a third of the body length, held low, with a black tip; slim, long-legged build
Canis latrans.difference: much slimmer and smaller than a wolf, with a narrower pointed muzzle and relatively larger ears; tail held low

Tamias striatus.marks: five dark stripes along the back: one down the spine and two on each side, with a pale buff stripe between the side pairs; reddish rump with no stripes; face with a pale stripe above and below the eye; tail flattened, about a third of the body length, not bushy; small rounded ears
Tamias striatus.difference: has stripes on the face (golden-mantled ground squirrel does not); rump reddish; smaller and slimmer

Tamiasciurus hudsonicus.marks: reddish-brown upperparts; white belly separated from the sides by a thin black line along the flank; white eye-ring; small ears, with short tufts in winter only; bushy tail shorter than the body, rusty above with a dark fringe; small squirrel, about half the weight of an Eastern Gray Squirrel
Tamiasciurus hudsonicus.difference: white eye-ring and black flank line; no long ear tufts; smaller than the Eurasian Red Squirrel

Felis catus.draw: adult domestic cat of the classic short-haired brown tabby type, walking
Felis catus.marks: brown-grey coat with dark mackerel stripes on the sides, rings on the legs and tail and an M mark on the forehead; long thin tail, ringed, with a dark tip, held up in a gentle curve; green-yellow eyes
Felis catus.difference: long ringed tail (bobcat: short bobbed tail); smaller, with no ear tufts or cheek ruff

Sciurus vulgaris.draw: adult of the common red form, in winter coat
Sciurus vulgaris.marks: bright rusty-red back, legs and tail; creamy white belly; long tufts of hair on the ear tips; bushy tail about as long as the body, raised in a curve over the back
Sciurus vulgaris.difference: red, with long ear tufts; smaller than the Eastern Gray Squirrel

Capreolus capreolus.draw: adult male (buck) in red-brown summer coat, with antlers
Capreolus capreolus.marks: small slender deer; short antlers, about the head length, upright and rough at the base, with usually three points each; black nose and muzzle with a white chin; no visible tail; white rump patch shaped like a kidney; large dark eyes
Capreolus capreolus.difference: much smaller; antlers short and upright, never flattened; no spots; no visible tail

Castor canadensis.marks: heavy, round-backed rodent with rich dark brown fur; broad flat paddle-shaped tail, black and scaly, about a third of the body length, held flat on the ground; large orange front teeth; small round ears; small eyes; large webbed hind feet
Castor canadensis.difference: far larger, with a broad flat paddle tail (muskrat: thin tail flattened from side to side)

Ursus americanus.draw: adult of the common black form
Ursus americanus.marks: black coat; brown muzzle; straight face profile from forehead to nose (no dish); tall, prominent rounded ears; no shoulder hump, the highest point of the back is over the hips; short curved claws
Ursus americanus.difference: no shoulder hump; straight face profile; taller ears; shorter claws than the brown bear

Didelphis virginiana.marks: grizzled grey body with long white guard hairs; white face with a long pointed pink nose; black, hairless rounded ears with pale tips; black legs; long naked tail, about the body length, black at the base and pink-white for the rest; pink feet with a clawless opposable thumb on the hind foot
Didelphis virginiana.difference: white face with a long pointed snout and a naked pink tail (brushtail possum: short face and a bushy black tail)

Marmota monax.marks: chunky, short-legged rodent; grizzled brown coat; dark brown to black feet; short, bushy, dark tail about a quarter of the body length; small rounded ears; blunt head; short dark claws
Marmota monax.difference: uniform grizzled brown with dark feet (yellow-bellied marmot: yellow belly, white band between the eyes)

Otospermophilus beecheyi.marks: grey-brown back speckled with pale flecks; a dark triangle between the shoulders bordered by silvery-white patches running onto the sides of the neck; bushy grey tail edged with white, about two thirds of the body length; white eye-ring; short ears
Otospermophilus beecheyi.difference: a dark shoulder triangle between two silvery side patches (rock squirrel lacks the silver shoulder patches)

Alces alces.draw: adult male (bull) with full palmate antlers
Alces alces.marks: very tall, dark brown to black deer, legs long and pale grey-brown; shoulder hump higher than the rump; long, overhanging bulbous muzzle; dewlap (bell) hanging from the throat; broad flat palmate antlers with points along the outer edge, spreading sideways; very short tail
Alces alces.difference: flattened palmate antlers spreading sideways; long overhanging nose and a dewlap; shoulder hump

Phoca vitulina.marks: spotted coat, grey to brown with many small dark spots and rings; short round dog-like head with a concave forehead and short muzzle; V-shaped nostrils; no external ear flaps; short front flippers with claws
Phoca vitulina.difference: rounded head and short muzzle with a dip at the forehead (grey seal: long straight Roman-nose profile); nostrils form a V

Cervus canadensis.marks: pale tan to golden-brown body with a much darker chocolate-brown neck, head and legs; shaggy dark mane on the throat; large pale buff rump patch with a short tail; antlers huge and sweeping back, about six points per side; large deer
Cervus canadensis.difference: paler body contrasting with a dark mane and head; larger, with a large pale rump patch (red deer: more uniform red-brown)

Ondatra zibethicus.marks: dense glossy dark brown fur, paler on the belly; long, scaly, nearly naked black tail flattened from side to side, about as long as the body; small ears almost hidden in fur; rat-like head with small eyes; partly webbed hind feet
Ondatra zibethicus.difference: smaller; tail flattened from side to side; no white muzzle or orange teeth

Sus scrofa.marks: dark grey-brown to black bristly coat with a mane of long stiff hairs along the spine; massive wedge-shaped head; long snout ending in a flat disc; short upward-curving tusks from the lower jaw; small erect ears; short legs; thin tail with a tuft, hanging down
Sus scrofa.difference: larger and darker, with tusks curving out and up, a long snout and no pale collar

Oryctolagus cuniculus.draw: adult wild-type rabbit, crouched on all four feet
Oryctolagus cuniculus.marks: grey-brown agouti fur with a rusty nape; long ears with thin black edges at the tips; white underside of the tail; large dark eyes; stocky, compact body
Oryctolagus cuniculus.difference: smaller, with shorter ears and hind legs; ears without the large black tips of the hare; eyes dark brown, not amber

Sylvilagus audubonii.draw: adult, crouched on all four feet
Sylvilagus audubonii.marks: pale buffy-grey coat; ears very long for a cottontail, about one and a half times the head length, sparsely furred inside; white cotton-ball tail; light brownish-yellow nape; slim body
Sylvilagus audubonii.difference: paler and greyer, with longer, thinner ears

Lynx rufus.marks: tawny to grey-brown coat with dark spots and bars, especially on the legs; short bobbed tail about the head length, black on the top of the tip and white below; short black ear tufts; ruff of fur on the cheeks; backs of the ears black with a white spot; long legs
Lynx rufus.difference: short bobbed tail, ear tufts and cheek ruff; about twice the size of a house cat

Mephitis mephitis.marks: glossy black body; thin white stripe down the middle of the forehead; a white cap on the nape that splits into two white stripes running back along the sides; very bushy black-and-white tail, held up; small head and ears; long front claws; short legs
Mephitis mephitis.difference: two broad white stripes along the back from a white nape cap (spotted skunks: smaller, with many broken white stripes and spots)

Phascolarctos cinereus.marks: dense ash-grey fur, white on the chest and inner arms; large round ears with white fluffy fringes; large black, rubbery, spoon-shaped nose; small eyes; no visible tail; strong limbs with long curved claws; stocky body
Phascolarctos cinereus.difference: big fluffy white-fringed ears and a large black nose; clinging in a tree (wombat: small ears, on the ground)

Erinaceus europaeus.marks: back covered in short brown-and-cream spines; face and belly covered in coarse brown fur; dark brown band across the chest; pointed snout with a black nose; small rounded ears; short legs
Erinaceus europaeus.difference: chest uniform brown, without the white patch of the Northern White-breasted Hedgehog

Megaptera novaeangliae.marks: black or dark grey body with a white throat and belly; extremely long flippers, about a third of the body length, mostly white with knobby front edges; knobs (tubercles) on the head and lower jaw; throat grooves; small dorsal fin on a hump two thirds of the way back; broad flukes with a jagged trailing edge
Megaptera novaeangliae.difference: very long white flippers and knobbed head; huge baleen whale with no beak and no teeth

Lepus europaeus.draw: adult, crouched on all four feet
Lepus europaeus.marks: tawny-brown grizzled coat with a rusty chest and white belly; very long ears with large black tips, longer than the head; amber-yellow eyes; long hind legs; tail black on top and white below
Lepus europaeus.difference: larger and longer-legged, with longer black-tipped ears and amber eyes

Urocyon cinereoargenteus.marks: grizzled silver-grey back; rusty orange neck sides, legs and flanks; white throat and cheeks; black stripe on the muzzle from the nose to the eye; bushy tail with a black stripe along the top and a black tip; shorter legs than a red fox
Urocyon cinereoargenteus.difference: grizzled grey back with rusty sides; black-tipped tail with a black mane along its top (red fox: orange with a white tail tip and black stockings)

Zalophus californianus.marks: dark chocolate-brown sleek body; raised bony crest on the forehead, often pale; small external ear flaps; long, dog-like muzzle with whiskers; long front flippers it stands on; hind flippers turned forward under the body
Zalophus californianus.difference: has small external ears and stands upright on long front flippers (harbor seal has no ear flaps and lies on its belly)

Myocastor coypus.marks: large rodent with coarse brown fur; white muzzle and whiskers; bright orange front teeth; long round, scaly, sparsely haired tail, about two thirds of the body length; small ears; webbed hind feet
Myocastor coypus.difference: round rat-like tail (not flat); white muzzle; smaller than a beaver

Dasypus mexicanus.marks: body covered in a grey-brown armoured shell with nine narrow movable bands across the middle; long pointed head shield; long upright ears; long tapering tail covered in rings of armour, about two thirds of the body length; short legs with strong claws
Dasypus mexicanus.difference: split from the Nine-banded Armadillo in 2023 and almost identical to it; draw the typical nine-banded shape, do not invent distinguishing marks

Macropus giganteus.marks: soft grey-brown coat, paler below; long thick tail with a dark tip; large ears; long narrow head; hairy muzzle between the nostrils and the lip; very long hind feet
Macropus giganteus.difference: paler silver-grey (western grey kangaroo: chocolate-brown face and darker brown coat)

Lontra canadensis.marks: long, sleek, low-slung body with glossy dark brown fur; silvery-grey throat and cheeks; thick, muscular tail tapering to a point, about two thirds of the body length; broad flat head; small round ears; whiskers on a broad muzzle; webbed feet
Lontra canadensis.difference: much larger, with a thick tapering tail and a pale throat (mink: smaller, with a slim bushy tail and a white chin spot)

Ovis canadensis.draw: adult male (ram) with full curl horns
Ovis canadensis.marks: brown coat with a large white rump patch and white muzzle; massive, heavy, ridged horns curling back, down and forward around the ear in a full curl; short dark tail; white back of the legs; stocky build
Ovis canadensis.difference: massive curling horns and a white rump (chamois: short hooked horns and a striped face)

Erethizon dorsatum.marks: stocky dark brown to black body with long yellow-tipped guard hairs on the back; quills mostly hidden but visible on the rump and thick tail; short blunt face; small eyes and ears; arched back; short legs with long curved claws
Erethizon dorsatum.difference: far larger, with long guard hairs over the quills and a thick quilled tail

Loxodonta africana.marks: huge grey animal; very large ears shaped like the map of Africa, covering the shoulders; long curved tusks; concave back dipping in the middle; trunk with two finger-like tips; wrinkled skin; sloping forehead
Loxodonta africana.difference: very large ears covering the shoulders and a dip in the back (Asian elephant: small ears and a rounded, humped back)

Otospermophilus variegatus.marks: large ground squirrel with mottled grey-brown speckled coat, often darker on the head and shoulders and more cinnamon behind; long bushy tail, nearly the body length, grey and white-edged; white eye-ring; short ears
Otospermophilus variegatus.difference: no silvery shoulder patches; larger, with a longer and bushier tail

Nasua narica.marks: brown coat, grizzled on the shoulders; very long, flexible, upturned snout; white markings on the muzzle and around the eyes; long tail with faint pale rings, held upright like a flagpole; small rounded ears; long legs
Nasua narica.difference: long upturned snout and long, faintly ringed tail held straight up; no black eye mask

Canis familiaris.draw: a typical medium-size short-haired dog of mixed breed, tan with white on the chest and feet
Canis familiaris.marks: medium build; ears semi-erect, folding at the tip; tail curved up; tan coat with white chest and paws
Canis familiaris.difference: a domestic dog, not a wild canid: broader head, folded ear tips, curled tail

Bos bison.marks: massive dark brown animal with a huge shoulder hump; long shaggy woolly hair on the head, shoulders and front legs, short hair on the hindquarters; large low-hung head with a beard; short black curved horns; short tail with a tuft
Bos bison.difference: huge shoulder hump and shaggy front half; small horns curving up (African buffalo: no hump, massive horns joined by a boss)

Callospermophilus lateralis.marks: a white stripe bordered with black along each side of the back; golden-russet head and shoulders (the mantle); no stripes on the face; white eye-ring; grey back between the side stripes; short bushy tail
Callospermophilus lateralis.difference: no stripes on the face; coppery mantle on the head and shoulders; larger and heavier than a chipmunk

Castor fiber.marks: heavy rodent with chestnut to dark brown fur; broad flat scaly paddle tail, narrower than the American beaver's; large orange front teeth; small ears; webbed hind feet
Castor fiber.difference: narrower tail; longer, narrower muzzle; often paler, more chestnut fur

Rattus norvegicus.marks: grey-brown coarse fur, paler grey belly; blunt muzzle; small furry ears that would not reach the eye if folded forward; thick scaly tail shorter than the head and body together; heavy-bodied
Rattus norvegicus.difference: stockier, with a blunter muzzle, smaller ears, and a tail shorter than the body (black rat: tail longer than the body, larger ears)

Antilocapra americana.marks: tan upperparts; white belly, rump patch and two white bands across the throat; black horns with a short forward prong and a hooked tip; black cheek patch and black muzzle; large eyes set high; slender legs
Antilocapra americana.difference: white throat bands and white rump; horns pronged with a hooked tip (impala: lyre-shaped horns, black stripes on the rump)

Tachyglossus aculeatus.marks: back and sides covered in cream spines with dark tips, mixed with brown fur; long thin tubular snout, about the head length, hairless; very short legs; large curved claws on the feet, hind feet pointing back; no visible tail
Tachyglossus aculeatus.difference: long thin beak-like snout; longer, cream spines; large backward-pointing hind claws

Trichosurus vulpecula.draw: adult of the common silver-grey form
Trichosurus vulpecula.marks: silver-grey fur, cream belly; large pointed ears; pink nose; bushy black tail with a bare grip patch under the tip; large dark eyes; fox-like face
Trichosurus vulpecula.difference: bushy black tail and large pointed ears (ringtail possum: tail white-tipped and thinner, ears small and round)

Neogale vison.marks: glossy dark chocolate-brown fur, almost black; small white patch on the chin; long, slim low body; short legs; bushy tail about half the body length; small rounded ears
Neogale vison.difference: much smaller, with a slim bushy tail and white chin spot

Lepus californicus.draw: adult, crouched on all four feet
Lepus californicus.marks: grey-buff coat speckled with black; very long ears, longer than the head, with black tips; tail with a black stripe along the top that runs onto the rump; long hind legs
Lepus californicus.difference: much larger, with longer ears and legs; black stripe on the tail and rump

Macaca fascicularis.marks: grey-brown to reddish-brown fur, pale below; long tail as long as the body or longer; pale whiskered cheeks and a crest of hair on the crown; pinkish-brown bare face with prominent brow; close-set eyes
Macaca fascicularis.difference: long tail and pale cheek whiskers; brownish, not green-grey; face pinkish-brown, not black

Equus quagga.marks: broad black and white stripes that wrap around the belly; pale brownish shadow stripes between the black stripes on the haunches; short upright mane striped like the body; black muzzle; striped legs fading below the knee
Equus quagga.difference: stripes over the whole body, wrapping around the belly; upright mane

Cervus elaphus.marks: red-brown coat, greyer in winter; shaggy neck mane; pale cream rump patch; branched antlers with many points and a crown of several points at the top; large deer
Cervus elaphus.difference: more uniform red-brown, with a smaller pale rump patch and a crown of points at the antler tips

Marmota flaviventris.marks: grizzled brown back; yellow-orange belly and neck sides; white band across the face between the eyes; buff patches beside the neck; bushy brown tail about a third of the body length; stocky build
Marmota flaviventris.difference: yellow belly and white face band (groundhog is uniform brown)

Tursiops truncatus.marks: grey body, darker on the back and paler on the belly; short thick beak clearly separated from the rounded melon by a crease; tall curved dorsal fin in the middle of the back; pointed flippers; mouth line curved in a smile
Tursiops truncatus.difference: small toothed dolphin with a short beak and tall curved dorsal fin

Talpa europaea.marks: cylindrical body with velvety black fur; huge spade-like front feet turned outward, pink with big claws; pointed pink snout; eyes tiny, hidden in fur; no external ears; short stubby tail
Talpa europaea.difference: huge spade front feet turned outward; no visible eyes or ears

Wallabia bicolor.marks: dark brown to black coat with a rusty-orange belly and chest; pale yellowish cheek stripe; dark feet and tail; stocky build
Wallabia bicolor.difference: much darker overall, with a dark tail and feet and a pale cheek stripe

Lepus americanus.draw: adult in brown summer coat, crouched on all four feet
Lepus americanus.marks: rusty-brown coat with white feet and belly; very large furry hind feet; ears shorter than other hares, with dark tips; short tail, brown above
Lepus americanus.difference: huge hind feet with white toes; larger body and dark-tipped ears

Sciurus griseus.marks: bright silver-grey back with no brown wash; pure white belly; very long bushy tail edged with white, raised over the back; large ears without tufts; dark feet
Sciurus griseus.difference: cleaner silver-grey with no brown; larger, with a longer and fuller tail

Panthera leo.marks: uniform tawny coat; large dark-golden mane around the head, neck and chest; long tail with a black tuft at the end; rounded ears with black backs; heavy muscular build
Panthera leo.difference: male has a big mane; tail with a black tuft; much larger

Pecari tajacu.marks: pig-like animal with coarse grizzled dark grey-black hair; pale whitish collar around the neck and shoulders; long snout ending in a disc; short thin legs; small ears; mane of long hair along the back; no visible tail
Pecari tajacu.difference: smaller, with a pale collar; straight, short tusks that do not show

Tamiasciurus douglasii.marks: dark olive-brown back; orange-tan belly; black line along the side between back and belly; orange eye-ring; bushy tail with dark centre and white fringe
Tamiasciurus douglasii.difference: darker olive-brown with an orange belly (American red squirrel: rusty with a white belly)

Meles meles.marks: grey body; white head with two broad black stripes running from the nose over the eyes to the ears; small white-tipped ears; black legs and chest; long-clawed front feet; short tail; low wedge-shaped build
Meles meles.difference: white face with black stripes through the eyes; grey body; short tail without rings

Aepyceros melampus.marks: reddish-brown back over a paler fawn band on the flanks; white belly; black stripes down each thigh and the tail; black tufts above the hind hooves; lyre-shaped ridged horns curving up and out; large ears with black tips
Aepyceros melampus.difference: lyre-shaped horns, black thigh stripes and black hoof tufts

Dasyprocta punctata.marks: rabbit-sized rodent with glossy orange-brown to chestnut fur, more grizzled on the front half; long slender legs; small hooflike claws; tiny tail; small rounded ears; arched back
Dasyprocta punctata.difference: much smaller, slim and long-legged, with orange-brown fur

Enhydra lutris.marks: dense dark brown fur; pale cream to grey head and neck in adults; round head with small ears; thick whiskers; flipper-like webbed hind feet; flattened tail about a third of the body length; small front paws held on the chest
Enhydra lutris.difference: floats on its back with a pale head and flipper-like hind feet

Ursus arctos.marks: brown coat, with paler tips on the guard hairs; large muscular hump over the shoulders; concave (dished) face profile; small rounded ears; long pale curved claws on the front feet
Ursus arctos.difference: shoulder hump, dished face, small ears and long claws

Halichoerus grypus.marks: dark grey to brown coat with paler blotches; long straight Roman-nose profile with no dip at the forehead; parallel nostrils; heavy body; no external ear flaps
Halichoerus grypus.difference: long straight muzzle and parallel nostrils; larger

Cynomys ludovicianus.marks: plump, tan ground squirrel with paler belly; short tail with a black tip; short legs; small ears; large dark eyes
Cynomys ludovicianus.difference: smaller and paler tan, with a black-tipped tail

Hydrochoerus hydrochaeris.marks: very large barrel-shaped rodent; coarse reddish-brown to grey-brown hair; large blunt square head; small round ears; eyes and nostrils set high; short legs; partly webbed feet; no visible tail
Hydrochoerus hydrochaeris.difference: huge and heavy, with a blunt square head and no tail

Blarina brevicauda.marks: dark slate-grey velvety fur; long pointed snout; tiny eyes; ears hidden in fur; short tail about a quarter of the body length; stout body; pink feet
Blarina brevicauda.difference: normal small front feet, not spade-like; short tail

Hippopotamus amphibius.marks: massive barrel body with smooth grey-brown skin, pinkish around the eyes, ears and on the belly; huge head with a broad muzzle; eyes, ears and nostrils set on top of the head; very short legs; short tail flattened from side to side
Hippopotamus amphibius.difference: huge, nearly hairless and barrel-shaped, with eyes and nostrils on top of the head

Pseudocheirus peregrinus.marks: grey to reddish-brown fur; white patches below the eyes and behind the ears; small rounded ears; long tapering prehensile tail, dark at the base and white for the last third, often curled at the tip
Pseudocheirus peregrinus.difference: thin tail with a white tip, curled at the end; small rounded ears

Syncerus caffer.marks: large black, sparsely haired body; massive horns joined in a heavy boss on top of the head, sweeping down and then up to the tips; drooping, fringed ears below the horns; heavy build; tail with a tuft
Syncerus caffer.difference: no hump and no shaggy mane; massive horns joined in a boss

Phacochoerus africanus.marks: grey, nearly naked body; mane of long coarse hair along the back; broad flat head with warty bumps on the face; two long tusks curving up and out from the mouth; thin tail held straight up when running
Phacochoerus africanus.difference: large curved upper tusks and warts on the face; almost hairless grey skin

Alouatta palliata.marks: black fur, with long golden-brown hair fringing the flanks (the mantle); large head with a bulging throat; bare black face; long prehensile tail as long as the body, curled at the tip
Alouatta palliata.difference: all black with a golden fringe on the flanks and a swollen throat; no white face

Equus caballus.draw: an adult bay horse of a typical light riding type
Equus caballus.marks: reddish-brown body with black mane, tail and lower legs; long flowing tail; long mane lying to one side; small white blaze on the face
Equus caballus.difference: no stripes; long flowing mane and tail

Dama dama.draw: adult male (buck) in spotted summer coat, with palmate antlers
Dama dama.marks: chestnut-brown coat with white spots along the back and flanks; white rump outlined in black, with a black-striped tail; flattened palmate antlers with points along the back edge; prominent Adam's apple
Dama dama.difference: larger, with white spots, a long tail and flattened antlers

Puma concolor.marks: plain tawny coat, paler below; small round head; long thick tail with a dark tip, about two thirds of the body length; black on the muzzle sides and the backs of the ears; long, muscular body
Puma concolor.difference: small head, no mane, long tail with a dark tip, no tuft

Giraffa giraffa.marks: very long neck and legs; irregular star-shaped brown blotches with jagged edges on a pale tan background, continuing down the legs; two short horn-like ossicones on the head; long tail with a black tuft; sloping back
Giraffa giraffa.difference: irregular, jagged blotches extending down the lower legs

Rupicapra rupicapra.marks: goat-like animal with tawny-brown summer coat; white face with a black stripe from the eye to the muzzle; short black horns that rise straight up and hook back at the tips; dark stripe along the back; sturdy legs
Rupicapra rupicapra.difference: short hooked black horns and a striped face

Bradypus variegatus.marks: shaggy grey-brown fur, often with a greenish tinge; small round head with a dark mask through the eyes and a pale face; permanent smile; three long curved claws on each foot; very short tail; long arms
Bradypus variegatus.difference: three claws on the front feet; dark eye mask and pale face

Sciurus aureogaster.draw: adult of the common grey-and-red form
Sciurus aureogaster.marks: grizzled grey back; bright rust-red belly; bushy tail grey frosted with white; white eye-ring; small ears
Sciurus aureogaster.difference: grey back with a deep red belly, and a grey white-frosted tail

Marmota marmota.marks: plump grey-brown rodent with a darker head; paler muzzle; short bushy tail with a dark tip; small rounded ears; short legs
Marmota marmota.difference: greyer, with a darker head and pale muzzle

Notamacropus rufogriseus.marks: grizzled grey back with a red-brown neck and shoulders; white stripe on the upper lip; black nose, paws and the tip of the tail; pale belly
Notamacropus rufogriseus.difference: red neck and shoulders, white lip stripe and pale grey body

Ochotona princeps.marks: small, egg-shaped body with grey-brown fur; large round ears edged with white; no visible tail; short legs; whiskers; dark eyes
Ochotona princeps.difference: much smaller, with round ears and no visible tail

Chlorocebus pygerythrus.marks: grizzled olive-grey fur; black face framed by a white band across the brow and white cheeks; long tail with a dark tip; pale belly; black hands and feet
Chlorocebus pygerythrus.difference: black face framed by white; olive-grey fur

Macropus fuliginosus.marks: chocolate-brown to grey-brown coat; dark brown face; paler belly; dark hands, feet and tail tip
Macropus fuliginosus.difference: darker brown coat and dark chocolate face

Connochaetes taurinus.marks: slate-grey body with dark vertical bands on the neck and shoulders; black shaggy mane and beard; long black tail; large head with a broad muzzle; horns curving out sideways and up like a cow's; front higher than the back
Connochaetes taurinus.difference: slimmer, with a beard, mane and thinner horns; body slopes down to the back

Canis lupus.marks: large, powerful canid with grizzled grey-buff coat; broad head with a broad muzzle; pale cheeks and throat; relatively small rounded ears; long legs; bushy tail held low with a dark tip
Canis lupus.difference: much larger, with a broad muzzle, smaller ears and a heavier build

Callosciurus erythraeus.marks: olive-brown back; dark reddish-chestnut belly; long bushy tail with faint rings, darker towards the tip
Callosciurus erythraeus.difference: olive back and dark red belly; no ear tufts

Mirounga angustirostris.marks: huge, tan to grey-brown body with a thick, scarred neck shield; large inflatable trunk-like nose hanging over the mouth; front flippers small; no external ear flaps
Mirounga angustirostris.difference: a huge male with a large trunk-like nose

Cebus imitator.marks: black body; white to cream face, throat and shoulders; black cap on the head; pinkish face; long prehensile tail, often curled at the tip
Cebus imitator.difference: white face and shoulders with a black cap

Tragelaphus strepsiceros.marks: grey-brown body with six to ten thin vertical white stripes on the sides; very long spiral horns with two and a half twists; white chevron between the eyes; large round ears; fringe of hair under the throat
Tragelaphus strepsiceros.difference: very long spiral horns and thin white side stripes

Rattus rattus.marks: dark grey-brown to black fur; pointed muzzle; large thin ears; slim body; tail longer than the head and body, uniform dark
Rattus rattus.difference: slimmer, with larger ears and a tail longer than the body

Erinaceus roumanicus.marks: back covered in brown-and-cream spines; face and belly brown; a distinct white patch on the chest; pointed snout; small ears

Kobus ellipsiprymnus.marks: shaggy grey-brown coat; white ring on the rump around the tail (or a white rump patch, depending on the form); white eyebrows and muzzle; white throat patch; long, heavily ridged horns that sweep back and up, then curve forward at the tips
Kobus ellipsiprymnus.difference: white ring around the rump, shaggy coat, and ridged horns curving forward at the tips (wildebeest: cow-like horns, black beard and mane)

Vombatus ursinus.marks: stocky, barrel-shaped body with coarse brown fur; broad flat head; small rounded ears; large, naked nose; very short legs; no visible tail
Vombatus ursinus.difference: small ears and a heavy, barrel-like body on the ground
